description: The certification cases a counterparty is tested against must be generated from the IPL model by region decomposition — each case traceable to a symbolic region of the model — rather than hand-written ad hoc.
name: ipl_cert_cases_from_decomposition

description: Region decomposition produces far more cases than can be executed exhaustively. Certification must run a deliberately selected subset of the generated cases — justified by a documented selection strategy and covering the required behaviour classes and risk-prioritised regions — not every generated case, and not an arbitrary few.
name: ipl_cert_cases_selected

description: Certification cannot be signed off while any selected certification case is failing; every conformance failure — whether in the counterparty or in the IPL model — must be resolved and re-run first.
name: ipl_cert_defects_resolved

description: In production, live sessions must be checked against the IPL model; any drift between specification and running system must surface as an observable failure and be resolved or raised as an incident.
name: ipl_cert_drift_monitored

description: Whatever subset of cases is selected, it must include invalid and rejection behaviour, not just happy paths — the IPL model's invalid message flows (validity violations and the expected reject responses) must be among the cases exercised.
name: ipl_cert_invalid_flows_tested

description: Each certification run must declare its mode — Simulator (against an IPL-generated simulator) or Proxy (in-line with the live venue) — so its scope and fidelity are on the record.
name: ipl_cert_mode_declared

description: Before sign-off the IPL model should be co-simulated against captured UAT or production traffic (the digital twin) to confirm the model and the real system agree.
name: ipl_cert_model_cosimulated

description: The IPL model must type-check and be free of errors before it is used to generate tests or simulators — only a valid model is guaranteed to produce a functioning implementation.
name: ipl_cert_model_valid

description: A certification sign-off must pin the exact IPL model version and the ROE version it formalizes, so the result is traceable to a specific formal specification.
name: ipl_cert_model_version_pinned

description: No counterparty is enabled in production without a prior IPL-based certification that passed and was signed off.
name: ipl_cert_no_onboarding_without_pass

description: A completed certification run must produce a certification report tying each verdict back to the IPL model's regions; a run that finishes with no report is not an auditable certification.
name: ipl_cert_report_produced

description: The venue's Rules of Engagement / FIX specification a counterparty is certified against must be formalized as an IPL model — an executable formal spec — before any certification run, not left as prose.
name: ipl_cert_roe_formalized
